leads.extracted_text: GPS is a global navigation system run by the U.S. Space Force. Around 31 satellites orbit at 20,200 km altitude, each broadcasting its precise location and atomic-clock time over microwave signals. A GPS receiver (your phone, your car) listens to at least 4 satellites, measures how long each signal took to arrive, and uses those four travel times to trilaterate latitude, longitude, altitude and its own clock offset. Modern phones combine GPS with Galileo (EU), GLONASS (Russia) and BeiDou (China) for better accuracy.
